title: etbb-july-2024-february-2026-update.pdf — section 456
text:
3. The term “Islamophobia” is used by some Muslims (and others) to refer to hate crime which
is targeted towards Muslims. There is no single agreed definition of Islamophobia, or even
agreement about whether the term is meaningful. The All-Party Parliamentary Group (APPG)
on British Muslims proposed the following definition:
“Islamophobia is rooted in racism and is a type of racism that targets expressions of
Muslimness or perceived Muslimness.”
435

4. This was not accepted by the previous government, with many contending that it is vague
and could be a threat to free speech, and exacerbate existing divisions. Furthermore, Islam
is multi-racial, and Muslims are not a race in line with the Equality Act (EqA) 2010’s definition
of race.
436

5. In 2025, a new working group was established to provide the government with a working
definition of Anti-Muslim Hatred/Islamophobia, aiming to balance experiences of
Islamophobia with a commitment to freedom of thought and expression.437
